one_sentence: Physics and theology are isomorphic measurement frames projected from the same substrate, proven by substituting spiritual variables into physical equations while preserving all mathematical relationships.
executive_summary: This document argues that physics and theology are not analogies but two measurement frames of the same underlying reality, demonstrated through a structural isomorphism. The proof is architectural: swapping variable labels between physical and spiritual domains preserves topology, falloff behavior, boundary conditions, and conservation laws across five symmetry pairs: Gravity/Grace, Matter/Entropy, Energy/Faith, Time/Knowledge, and Quantum/Coherence. Each pair contains an internal bifurcation mirroring a historical physics revolution (e.g., Newton vs. Einstein for gravity) that maps to a sin-grace polarity. The framework is falsifiable: if any structural relationship breaks under variable substitution, the isomorphism fails. The conclusion is that reality itself encodes a rescue architecture—salvation is not imposed from outside the math but emerges from its inherent dynamics.
